doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Liner notes, personnel lists and exploring discographies
summary: He read liner notes and personnel as a youth, and enjoys tracing names such as Manny Klein through the discography.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Were you — this is a bit of a tangent but — when you were growing up were you an avid reader of LP liner notes?

Yes, although I was an avid reader of everything. Everything. If you look back to liner notes back in the day in more cases than not the liners were pretty top of line, they really weren’t, you know, as exhaustive. Let’s say something like what Bill Evans did for “Kind of Blue.” Okay? Because he was involved of course in the recording too. But I would read them. You know who’s the personnel? That was always a big thing too.

Me too. And you had mentioned before we were recording how the tangents in the music world and how it’s all this connection and I remember seeing, “Oh Clark Terry’s on this record and he was on that other record” and all these just like musical chairs I’d have to say.

Without a doubt. One of the things that I enjoy doing, I’m sure you’re familiar with Tom Lawrence Jazz Discography, which is a great, great, great resource, especially for a historian or a writer or what-have-you. But it’s always interesting to go in and plug in a name and go back to their early days, okay? I did this recently again with Manny Klein who was a great, great, great trumpet player, great guy, great sense of humor, they’d always make fun of his nose, he made fun of his nose you know. But you go back and you find out that Manny Klein played on all of these records from the 20s, this was before he went to Hollywood you know.
